Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the transparency on traffic patterns and the governance constraints. Below is a concise recap of the key pain points, our proposed pilot approach, and the immediate next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Spiky inference volume at end-of-month reporting windows (sustained 60–90 req/s peaks, short bursts to 200 req/s) causing occasional latency tails (99th pctl > 800ms).
- Regulatory requirement to isolate PII processing into a customer-only environment (separate pool + audit trail).
- Procurement wants a clear SLA, procurement checklist, and a one-page mutual action plan for internal signoff.
- Desire to cap token/compute spend and avoid noisy-neighbor tail latency during business hours.

Goals for a successful pilot
- Pilot a dedicated pool sized for typical mid-month load: target steady throughput 80 req/s, headroom for bursts to 200 req/s via burst policy.
- Isolation: dedicated tenant lane (no multi-tenant co-tenants), VPC peering and customer-managed ingress for data residency.
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile <= 250ms for sub-512 token inference in pilot configuration; target 99th <= 150ms in steady-state after optimizations.
- Ops: canary rollout, rollback policy, and on-call war room playbook during first 72 hours.

Proposed technical outline (pilot)
- Initial reserved pool: 4 GPUs (A100-class equivalents) for pilot with option to commit to 8 GPUs for production.
- Autoscale: burst capacity (+50% for short windows) with pre-authorized burst credits to avoid procurement delays.
- Model variant: recommend INT8 quantized variant for production; pilot can start with FP16 to validate quality.
- Caching & batching: enable prefix/KV caching and adaptive batching for low-latency online inference.

Deliverables I will send (attached)
- MAP_MedShift_onramp.xlsx — mutual action plan with milestones and owners.
- MedShift_NonProd_SLOs.pdf — suggested SLO language and monitoring hooks.

Immediate asks / owners
- Alex / Priya: confirm procurement timeline (target PO by end of July?) and procurement contact for contract redlines.
- Alex: confirm whether MedShift requires SOC2 in-scope or any additional attestation for pilot test data.
- Ben (eng): estimate for canary window and SRE support hours for pilot (Ben to follow up below).

Next call
- Proposed: Mon 6/21 10:00 PT — technical handoff (Ben + infra + your procurement).

Thanks — I’ll drop the MAP and the SLO doc now.

Adding technical clarifications and ops commitments from our side.

- Billing / burst credits: burst will be consumed from pre-authorized burst pool tied to the committed contract; bursts beyond the pre-authorized window are billed at burst rate (per-GPU-hour) and weCap with a soft throttle if requested. We will include explicit billing examples in the quote.
- Isolation: we will provision a dedicated tenancy lane (namespace + isolated GPU pool) with separate KV cache and tag-based audit logs for all inference requests. VPC peering for private data paths supported; if MedShift requires on-prem connector we can scope that as an add-on.
- Canary: recommend a 48–72 hour canary with synthetic traffic plus traffic shadowing of 5% of live traffic for first 24 hours. Rollback on any sustained >10% increase in error rate or if 99th pctl exceeds 350ms for longer than 15m.
- Ops support: SRE will provide a 2-day on-call window for the pilot start, and a runbook handoff. We estimate ~32 engineering hours across infra/SRE for pilot onboarding.

Attaching a short excerpt from our ops playbook that outlines rollback triggers and contact escalation.
